newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek minister calls for restraint on rates.
newsitem.headline: Greek minister calls for restraint on rates.

text.p: Greece's National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou called on commercial banks to show restraint in deposit rate reductions.
"Interest rate reductions should be in tandem with inflation," said Papandoniou. "Interest rate cuts should not outpace the deceleration of inflation."
CPI inflation fell to 6.0 percent year-on-year from 6.6 percent in February.
"The Greek economy suffers from excessive confidence," said Papandoniou, referring to an aggressive interest rate stance of some credit institutions.
Banks were correct to discount future favourable developments but self-restraint should be applied, he added.
He said the rate of growth of tax revenues increased in March, and he would have final figures next week.
